request.authored_statement: Admission correctly blocked a claim when its deterministic baseline exceeded the candidate limit and preserved those baseline IDs without constructing a request. Execution then rejected every no-request observation carrying evidence IDs, aborting the entire shadow artifact and HTML generation before other claims could be observed.

candidates.added_code:
def test_blocked_and_empty_admissions_remain_typed_observations(
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
                deterministic_evidence_ids=("E:baseline:1", "E:baseline:2"),
    assert bundle.observations[0].deterministic_evidence_ids == (
        "E:baseline:1",
        "E:baseline:2",
    )

    artifact_path = write_shadow_execution(bundle, tmp_path / "blocked.json")
    assert load_shadow_execution(artifact_path) == bundle

    artifact = json.loads(artifact_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    artifact["observations"][0]["deterministic_evidence_ids"].append(
        "E:baseline:1"
    )
    _assert_invalid_artifact(
        tmp_path,
        artifact,
        "blocked shadow evidence IDs must be non-empty and unique",
    )

    with pytest.raises(
        ValueError,
        match="only blocked shadow observations may preserve evidence IDs",
    ):
        replace(
            bundle.observations[1],
            deterministic_evidence_ids=("E:invented",),
        )

request.authored_statement: A blocked admission may preserve its deterministic baseline IDs without representing them as request candidates. The exception is limited to matching blocked admission/execution states; IDs must be non-empty, unique, and no more numerous than eligible evidence. Empty and every other no-request observation continue to reject evidence IDs. Serialization and loading enforce the same contract.
